name: tier0_corridor_junction
_comment: Tier 0 review corridor. Geometry is authored here rather than in code so the junction
SHAPE: a one-tile-wide vertical trunk with a one-tile-wide horizontal branch crossing it
to form a four-way junction three tiles ahead of the player.
TWO THINGS HERE ARE LOAD-BEARING AND WERE BOTH GOT WRONG ON THE FIRST CAPTURE:
1. CORRIDORS ARE ONE TILE WIDE. A three-wide carve is a room, not a corridor: every cell
in it has three or more open neighbours, so the junction check passes trivially and the
scene stops testing what it claims to. Width is what makes a junction a junction.
2. THE JUNCTION MUST SIT INSIDE THE LIT RADIUS. The critic is asked which way they would
walk. With the junction at 6 tiles and the carried light reaching 5.5, the first capture
put the choice in the dark and the question could not be answered at all. It is placed
at 3 tiles here. If light.radius_tiles in harness_config.yaml is reduced below ~4, this
spec must move the junction closer or the scene silently stops posing its question.
Both arms are geometrically symmetric, so any preference the critic reports comes from the
floor and wall art rather than from the layout. Both run out past the lit radius so the
corridor reads as continuing rather than as a closed box.
Coordinates are tiles, (0,0) top-left. The outer ring stays solid wall. The camera centres
on the player, giving a visible rect of roughly 10x14 tiles.
